utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. As we enter the courtroom, we were told by the Registrar that today is the 200th trial date. Yes, if the witness could take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mesanovic. If you could be seated and make yourself comfortable. Yes, Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, can you please state your full name.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Kerim Mesanovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: As we discussed, part of your evidence in this case will be submitted in writing and we first need to deal with the formalities associated with that submission. You provided statements and information to representatives of the Office of the Prosecutor and you've testified before the ICTY in three trials, the Slobodan Milosevic case, the Kvocka et al. trial, and the Brdjanin trial. You have recently had an opportunity to review an amalgamated statement which contained portions of your testimony which you gave in the Kvocka case in 2000 and the Brdjanin case in 2002; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, could I have 65 ter 90285 on the screen, please. And if we could go to the next -- page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, is this the document which you reviewed the other day?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Can you confirm that the testimony provided by you which is contained in the amalgamated statement is accurate?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If you were asked today about the same matters contained in the amalgamated statement, would you provide the same information to the Trial Chamber, and that is, even if you couldn't formulate everything in the same words, the essence would be the same?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender the 65 ter number 90285, which is the amalgamated statement of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P3528, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And with Your Honours leave, I'll now read a short summary of the witness's evidence. The witness, Kerim Mesanovic, grew up in the town of Prijedor in the municipality of Prijedor. Prior to the conflict, he worked in the mobilisation department of the Municipal Secretariat for National Defence for over 10 years. He was dismissed from his employment on the 22nd of May, 1992. He was brought back to his job for a short time and given a freedom of movement pass. On the 24th of June, 1992, the witness was arrested and placed in a cell at the Prijedor SUP, or the public security station, which is Schedule C, 20.1. He was placed in the cell with a number of other men. These men, including the witness, were beaten at the Prijedor SJB, before being transferred to the Omarska camp, which is Schedule 20.-- Schedule C, 20.2. The witness had four teeth knocked out. The witness was detained in the Omarska camp until early August 1992. He was first placed in the "White House" for the -- for three days of his detention. Zeljko Mejakic then ordered him to be taken to the "glass house" in the administration building. The witness described the condition at the Omarska camp, other beatings and killings, and this is Schedule B, Incident 15.2. He also gave evidence about the killing of a number of men and women that were taken from the Omarska camp, and this is Schedule B, 15.3. The witness also testified about the killing of a large number of men from the Brdo area at the Omarska camp, and this is Schedule B, Incident 15.4. Mr. Mesanovic was transferred to Trnopolje camp on the 6th of August, 1992. The following day, he returned to his home. He then went to the village of Petrov Gaj in the Prijedor municipality where he stayed until the second half of September. He obtained fake identification which enabled him to travel to Novi Sad. And he went there -- from there to a third country. The witness describes the destruction of religious sites in Prijedor municipality, which is Schedule D, Incident 17, and the destruction of non-Serb property. That completes the summary of the witness's written evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, I have a few questions for you. You testified that you were initially dismissed from your job in the mobilisation department on the 22nd of May, 1992, and you testified about a number of -- the numbers for the military units, and this is at paragraph 9 on pages 11 and 12 of the amalgamated statement. I'd now like you to look at a document.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And if I could have 65 ter number 05745 on the screen, please. If we could go to page 2 in the English and also page 2 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, you see there that these are minutes of the fourth meeting of the Council for National Defence of the Prijedor Municipal Assembly held on the 15th of May, 1992. And at paragraph 4 on page 2, it says, "In the assignment" -- this is talking about mobilisation: "In the assignment of the remaining conscripts to units, priority is to be given to the reinforcement of War Units 4777 and 8316." At the date of this meeting, you were still employed in the mobilisation department. What do you recall in relation to mobilisation and in particular in relation to these two war units?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Both these units were typically local units of Prijedor. The 4777 is a motorized brigade, manned 100 per cent from the Prijedor area. The territorial brigade was also manned 100 per cent by Prijedor conscript as the previous one. Given that the approximate proportion of ethnicity corresponded to the composition of the units, the units were in fact halved due to the absence of Serbs. And there were also some Serbs on the records who did not get any assignments. My former colleague Cedo Sipovac then came along who, in the pre-war period, became commander of a TO organ, which was a kind of counterpart for the Secretariat for National Defence. He came and asked for a list of Serb conscripts to be made in order for them to do something about it, and he also asked me to draw up call-out papers regardless of the residence addresses. We just needed to put inside the names, the address, the date of birth, and then he would serve those papers to those people who had not been conscripted yet, and I'm talking exclusively about Serbs.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please slow down. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, did you hear the interpreters asking that you please slow down in your speech?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Okay. They've requested that you do that.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm sorry. I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: In relation to War Unit 4777, you said that that was the motorized brigade. Is that more commonly known as the 43rd Motorized Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was the 43rd Motorized Brigade. In fact, before the war it was the 43rd Brigade, and later on the word "motorized" was added. That happened when the war broke out because some units were added to it in order to make it a motorized brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And in relation to the unit 8316, you said it was the Territorial Defence. Is that also known as the 5th Kozara Brigade?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And in the week prior to you being dismissed from your employment, did you assign the conscripts to these units?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If we could go to page 1, please, in the B/C/S and the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Under the words "ad 1" and at paragraph 1 there, we can see: "The draft of the decision on the organization and functioning of the Crisis Staff is approved, under the proviso that a representative of the garrison in Prijedor be added to the proposed list of the members of the Crisis Staff." Were you aware of whether a member, a representative of the Prijedor garrison was on the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I think that we are talking here about Radmilo Zeljaja who was assigned to the Crisis Staff before the war. He was a Captain First Class. And after the take-over of power, he became a major. And I think that he became also member of the Crisis Staff, as you've said. There was also possibly the man called Vladimir Arsic as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3529, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, I wish to show you another document. This was shown to you in your previous testimony, and this is at footnote 38 to paragraph 16 on page 21 of the amalgamated statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I could have 65 ter number 01046 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, this is a précis of minutes of the SDS Municipal Board meeting held on the 9th of May, 1992, and if I can draw your attention to the text under "Milan Kovacevic, president of the Municipal Assembly Executive Committee," where it says: "The cabinet meets daily and has adopted at least 50 decisions, the most important of which include: Replacement of staff has been carried out, with all SDA leaders removed from the functions in the Municipal Assembly; the functioning of government at the level of Krajina can now be felt; and instructions and decisions are being forwarded from the top." Is this consistent with your knowledge of events in -- at this time in early May 1992?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, particularly item number 1, the removal of all SDA officials from all offices.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And with respect to the replacement of staff being carried out, you were taken to a number of decisions in the Brdjanin case, and they are at paragraph 65 of your amalgamated witness statement. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I -- this was listed as an associated exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3530, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And, Mr. Mesanovic, the final document I wish to show you is another document that was shown to you in your previous testimony in the Brdjanin case, and this is at footnote 128 at paragraph 65 on page 76 of the amalgamated statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And, Mr. Registrar, if I could have 65 ter number 14808.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Sir, this is an order from the president of the Prijedor Crisis Staff. If I could draw your -- sorry, dated 2nd of July, 1992. And if I can draw your attention to paragraph 1 of the order: "All organs, enterprises, and communities are ordered to terminate the employment of workers who have participated in the armed rebellion and who are currently in Omarska and Keraterm." What happened in respect of your own employment? Were you provided with any information as to why you were being terminated?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: My employment was terminated on 22nd of May, 1992. I received a decision in which it reads that I was dismissed from my job due to acts committed against the state and the people. However, I was reinstated in June and I remained there until the 24th of June, when I was arrested. This decision dates from July, probably with the aim of confirming of what had already been done in May for the majority of people. I don't know about the rest of them, because by that time I was already in Omarska. So this decision covers the acts they made and issued in May and June.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And there you're referring to terminating the employment of workers?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Those were exclusively non-Serbs. There was seven Muslims and a female colleague who was married to a Muslim, so eight people were laid off. On the 22nd of May, it was explained to us that that was done due to the state of war, that nobody was going to be -- that we will have to stand by because they didn't have any instructions from the JNA. We were dismissed, whereas two people who had been in retirement were called to come back to work, two Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's an associated exhibit, and I seek to tender that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3531.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, they are all the questions I have for you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you are minded to tender all the associated exhibits listed in the list, I would like you to deal with two more documents on the same vein, which are 65 ter number 5764 and 21203. The witness just confirmed what is written, but wasn't asked any question about those two documents. Otherwise, are there any objections, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, I won't seek to use time taking the witness to 05764. And the same for 21203, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Mesanovic, your evidence in the previous trial was admitted in its entirety in this case and you will be further asked by Mr. Karadzic in his cross-examination. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. Good morning, Excellency. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning Mr. Mesanovic.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, is it true that you have finished the school for reserve officers in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And thereafter you were transferred to the reserve force of the JNA; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No. At that time we had two infantry reserve schools. That was in Bileca at the federal level and -- and Tuzla at the republican level. So we took care to assign TO officers to TO units. As you know, the TO and the JNA constituted the armed forces as a whole because they were all part of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you were within this Territorial Defence component of the joint armed forces?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have to remind both you and myself to make a pause between questions and answers in order to avoid causing problems for the interpreters, but also for the Prosecution and the Chamber. So were you then transferred to the reserve force or, given the nature of your job, were you in a position of an active-duty officer in the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I was employed with the Secretariat for National Defence where I received my war time assignment which was actually a work obligation, which means that during the war I continued doing my previous job and work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I think that you mentioned somewhere that you had been stationed at an airport. Did I understand that correctly? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No. The Prijedor detachment of this 8924 unit, but just don't hold me to it - it was called a detachment anyway - was stationed at the airport. The main task is for this detachment to defend Prijedor in case of an attack on the town. Since the war, turmoil was spreading all around us. I thought that if we are to defend the town of Prijedor, I --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the last part of his sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, the interpreters couldn't catch your last part of your answer. Could you repeat it, after you said, "I thought that if we are to defend the town of Prijedor ..." and then what did you say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thought that if we were to defend Prijedor, I simply had to be assigned to this TO detachment, defending Prijedor from everyone, not anyone in particular.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you bear in mind kindly that since your words have to be translated, please put a pause after you heard the question put by Mr. Karadzic. Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you given a rank upon completion of the reserve officers school?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Upon successful completion of the school for reserve officers, the rank of reserve second lieutenant is conferred.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it's a rank of a commissioned officer, not of a non-commissioned officer; right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, of a commissioned officer. And I became reserve captain right before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that between the period when you served your military service and did the reserve officers school you were called to attend various exercises and drills and in the process were given the rank of a captain?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you take an oath as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you also take an oath when you were given your first rank?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So it was the initial oath that was still valid?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who did you pledge your allegiance to?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the then-federal -- Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You were aware of the fact that the SFRY Presidency just before the multi-party elections issued a decision to withdraw the weapons of the TO and their storage into JNA warehouses; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this in fact done in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why was it then that in February of 1991 at a meeting of the Assembly one of the items on the agenda was a discussion as to why the SFRY Presidency order to hand over the weaponry to the Zarko Zgonjanin barracks had not been honoured?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. What I do know is that the TO staff depot was already housed in the Zarko Zgonjanin barracks. I don't know why that part of the order was not complied with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you recall that as part of these discussions -- did you attend this meeting at all?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was it not an item of the agenda that required your presence there?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that the orders came from the federal Secretariat for National Defence, and then through the secretariat in Sarajevo for the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and then from there on to Banja Luka, and from Banja Luka to Prijedor; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that before the elections there had been no Ministry of Defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No. There was no ministry, but it was called the Republican Secretariat for the National Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You also say in your 2000 statement, which does not bear your signature, that the municipality could not modify orders coming from the republican secretariat in a state of war and that the municipality enjoyed such a degree of autonomy that it was able to issue a definitive decision calling for mobilisation; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I can't give you a yes or no answer. I need to give you an explanation, with your leave, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, could you explain to me why you can't give an answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The municipality could defer the call-up for mobilisation only where the economy of that municipality would be threatened because such a large number of people would be called to attend. Other than that, the municipality did not enjoy any sort of autonomy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But in your statement you say that the municipality could refuse to comply with or it could modify a mobilisation order save in a time of war; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You confirmed in the case against Milosevic - let me say President Milosevic because there was a General Milosevic as well, to avoid any confusion - that you were aware of the fact that the SDA and Izetbegovic issued an order to the Muslims reservists that they should not respond to call-ups; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I heard it on the radio and television. And as for my being aware of it otherwise, well, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You are familiar with our laws, Law on the Army, on the Defence, and the All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I am, yes, to a certain degree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. An order not to respond to a call-up from the army, does that not constitute a crime?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that Stjepan Maric, a Croat and an associate of yours, was sent to Manjaca because he refused to have failed to act upon mobilisation call-ups; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No. And I'm sorry, Your Honours, I can't stop at that. I have to give you an explanation as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Stjepan Maric was not sent to Manjaca because he failed to perform his duties. He was accused as a chief of communications centre of having conveyed information to the Croats of where the JNA positions were. That was why he was sent to Manjaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But in your statement, in your amalgamated statement at page 31131, in answer to the question of whether he had been sent to Manjaca because he failed to execute these mobilisation orders, you say that he worked in the Ministry of Defence or the defence department as a computer expert and that he was sent to Manjaca as a regiment commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No, no. It must have been a mistake in interpretation or something like that, because I never said that. He was never a regiment commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. We will not be calling it up if you think it was misinterpretation. But is it true that you said in the case against President Milosevic that he had been accused of having misappropriated 100.000 German marks from the Croats and that that was the reason why he was sent to Omarska, and not because he was a Croat?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: That was the charge, that he, together with me, had taken 100.000 German marks and that we had taken a CD to Zagreb to -- we had taken a CD containing information to Zagreb and that was published in newspapers, that we had been given this money from Tudjman in exchange for information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you say that there were no more orders arriving from Sarajevo, instead they started arriving from Knin; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Am I right in saying that there was a change in the military's territorial structure and that the 2nd Military District was given a different area of responsibility and that the Banja Luka area came under the Knin Corps?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. That's part of your position and ideology. Officially there was the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, there was the republican secretariat, which should have been under the Banja Luka military district as the ultimate authority and decision-making structure for the republic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say this was part of my -- this is part of my position or ideology. Do you wish to say that in 1991 I was able to be in command of the Yugoslav People's Army and have an impact on its military territorial structure?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No. I apologise, I didn't mean you personally. I meant your side. Because you changed everything without having sat at official meetings and without having gone through the official Yugoslav organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was there in 1991 an SFRY Presidency, and was it not the supreme commander? I think that should suffice, the two questions.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: It was supposed to be the supreme commander of the armed forces of Yugoslavia, but we all know what happened instead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that the military territorial structure did not correspond to the republican borders; rather, it spilled over these borders so that one military district encompassed several republics?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that Muharem Efendic, a Muslim who was the commander of the barracks in Prijedor, was replaced by a Serb, Colonel Arsic, in 1991; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you allude to the fact that there were many more such cases without, in effect, giving any specific examples, save for the Efendic/Arsic replacement.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't understand. That there were more such cases in what sense?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You indicated that Muslim officers were being replaced by Serb officers; however, other than the Efendic/Arsic case, you mention no other case in relation to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't recall if I used the plural. It was a long time ago. But Prijedor was not a large military post. There may have been six or seven active-duty officers at most. Muharem Efendic was the commander of the barracks who was replaced by Arsic. That much is true. But a new person came, Radmilo Zeljaja who, admittedly, replaced Bosko Divjak.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So Zeljaja, as a Serb, came to replace a Serb; right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to read out for you now the names of the most important officials in the Prijedor municipality in March of 1992, and then please confirm or deny what I'm saying. Was the president of municipality Muhamed Cehajic a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Vice-president of the municipality Dr. Milomir Stakic, a Serb?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: President of the Executive Committee Dr. Mico Kovacevic, a Serb?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Vice-president of the Executive Economy Dr. Enes Kursumovic, a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Secretary of the Executive Committee Husein Basic, a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Chief of the public security station Enes Stanudzic [phoen], a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Esad Talundzic. Esad Talundzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A Muslim?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Chief of the Secretariat for National Defence Becir Medunjanin, a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Police Commander Fikret Kadiric, a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Commander of Territorial Defence Sakib Besic, a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: President of the court Nedzad Saric, a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Seric, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Municipality Prosecutor Omer Keranovic [phoen], a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Public defender Eso Mehmedagic, a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I think Novo Savic and his deputy Jasminka Begic, if I remember well, Predrag Novo Savic was the municipality public defender.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. That's ten to two or nine to three. That would be the ratio if what you're saying is true.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but you failed to mention other institutions. There were other local bodies in Prijedor. That was the state of play in the wake of the elections that were held based on the seats won and the inter-party agreement. As far as I know. I was never involved in these issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that in the old socialist system as well as in the new system it was customary for the chief of the public security station and the police station commander not to be of the same ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. But now that you've asked me about it, I will give you an answer. The first Muslim chief of the SUP -- the first Muslim to become chief of the SUP was in the 80s, and the first Muslim to become president of the municipality was also in the 80s, never before. The mine manager was never a Muslim. A post office director was never a Muslim. The manager of the local bank was never a Muslim. Et cetera, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that there came about a huge crisis because the police commander was supposed to be a Serb since the chief of that station was a Muslim, but this was not honoured and this brought about a major crisis in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I know that Predrag [as interpreted] Kadiric was a pre-war police commander, so he was not the result of those national parties attending the elections. He had been in that post for a long time before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But then the chief of the station should have been a Serb, because those two posts should have gone to one each, to each of the communities, not to one?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I wasn't a member of the SDA, I wasn't a member of the SDS, so I don't know what the parties agreed. I don't know about that, and I don't know the laws that were in force between the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you saw in the media and in the Kozarski Vjesnik periodical and in the news that there was a crisis lasting for a whole year because a Serb could not have been appointed to the post of the commander of the traffic police either; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I cannot remember who the commander of the traffic police was now. I can't remember that now. Media is the media.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And here I refer to only those functions that are important for defence and for security - the court posts, the prosecutor's posts of the police, and people's defence. This segment in Prijedor was in this ratio nine or ten Muslims to two or three Serbs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the way you presented it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you also confirmed that it is correct that Kosarac had its own Territorial Defence unit; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: You asked me about Kozarska, but all the local communes had their own. Lubija [phoen], Omarska, Kosarac, they all had their own units.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to speak a bit louder or to sit closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The interpreters are having problems with the names of the localities. Could you please repeat them. But generally saying, you said that each local commune had their own unit?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Each local office. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And when -- you are asked -- being asked by the interpreters to come closer to the microphone or speak a bit louder. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Each local office, and you know that the local office covered a number of local communes, the local office is like a small municipality, so each office had its own TO unit, and this was something that was structured even before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And so this is something that is a result of the Law on All People's Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And now you are talking about the military territorial organ being introduced, and am I correct if I say that the municipal Secretariat for National Defence is a civilian organ in the defence structure, with a command and control line that ends at the federal Secretariat for the National Defence, namely the federal -- the ministry; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And am I correct if I say that the military territorial organ is a military organ and that the line of command and control ends at the General Staff of the JNA or of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with that area, because the military territorial organ was a new institution which was supposed to start functioning shortly before the war. I was supposed to be a member of that VTO, that's how we referred to it. And my colleague Muhamed Burazerovic [as interpreted] and my colleague Dzevad Habibovic too; however, we did not pass the background check. There was some kind of snag there, so the three of us did not get in. But when you look at the composition of the VTO, the military territorial organ that you were talking about before, it was now 100 per cent Serbs. All the employees in the VTO were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But does not the name itself, the military territorial organ, say that it is a military organ that follows the military line of command and does not report to the Ministry of Defence, a part of which you were?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I should have said that, but I didn't have the opportunity to familiarise myself with all of that because war had already started then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. All right. Now, you say that it was quite tense, and you spoke a lot about that in your unsigned statement of 2000, on page 2, that there were tensions in the municipal committee for National Defence. Do you remember that in the early 1991, actually, in the summer of 1991, the president of the municipality, Juhajic, and the party president, SDA party, Mujadzic, actively hindered the movement of JNA through the municipality, placing some obstacles and entering into discussions with the JNA? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do. If I remember well, the main reason Mirsad Mujadzic faced the JNA units was because they had taken tanks into the streets of Prijedor, and their tracks were not rubber. They were not protected tracks. They had left the military ramp, and that was the main reason he did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So do you know that the president of the municipality ex officio is the president of the National Defence Council?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And is it true that it was not just the president of the party, but also the president of the municipality, Muhamed Juhajic, who also came out to deal with that action when obstacles were placed to the JNA?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I really cannot answer that question because I don't know about Muhamed Juhajic. I know about Mirsad. There weren't any obstacles involved. He just placed his own private vehicle there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you say that the last regular mobilisation of the TO took place in the spring of 1991 and then you said that Muslims were receiving M-48s and the Serbs were getting automatic rifles. Can you please tell me, tell all of us, who decided to differentiate between Serbs and Muslims regarding defence matters? Was this something that happened at the local level, at the federal level, at the military or the civilian level?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see six or seven questions here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you hear that, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I agree. But had I more time, there would be fewer questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So did you say that the last regular mobilisation was in the spring of 1991, and did you say that the weapons issued were different?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: The last mobilisation that took place was in 1991, without rifles. The second question, rifles were distributed, and I'm talking about the detachment we were talking about a couple of minutes before. In the same detachment there were automatic and semi-automatic rifles distributed to the Serbs, and M-48s were distributed to the Muslims. I'm talking about the detachment, when mobilisation had already been carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And, now, let's see, the local level -- was it the local level or was it the federal level that decided to differentiate between Serbs and Muslims in matters of defence?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, how can I answer this question? I don't think it was the federal level, because they couldn't come down to Prijedor. But I think that this came from the TO staff. And I know you will ask me because Sakib Bekic [as interpreted] was the commander but Rade Javoric was there too and Vrdar and tons of others. It was Sakib Besic and Vahid Ceric in the TO staff, and the rest were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But Vahid and Sakib, well, the participants don't know our names, they are Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they are Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And one of them was the chief of the TO; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Sakib Besic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And, please, can you tell us if you know when the SDA party adopted a negative stance in relation to the JNA and the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I wasn't a member of the party, so I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you are aware that Muslim leaders decided, advised, and even ordered Muslims not to take part in the mobilisation, not to respond to the summons for mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I did hear that. But I don't see anything bad in not going to war and not spilling blood. I don't believe that that is a crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And why do armies exist, Mr. Mesanovic?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Excellent question. The Yugoslav People's Army was formed and established in order to defend its people from the outside enemy, not from constituents of the JNA or from friends and relatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you recall what was the constitutional task of the JNA, defence of the territorial integrity of Yugoslavia and even the defence of the system of self-management; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I think that that was more the job of the police, a systemic task. The system was defended by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the territorial integrity was defended by the army and it did not require anyone's order to do that; this was its constitutional task. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: And from the outside enemy. I don't think that it was ever defined in the constitution that we should be fighting amongst ourselves, but that we should defend ourselves from outside enemies and in that way we defend our own territorial integrity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can internal forces also endanger the territorial integrity in an unconstitutional way?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I already said that as far as I can recall from the constitution this was the job of the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You are also aware that the police really was charged with terrorist and other acts to the extent that it was able to deal with them; but when republican armies are created that are exceeding the power and capacity of the police, then that is something that the army can do?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: If the republican armies exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So this decision not to respond to the call-up for mobilisation, this decision by the Muslims, who made this decision? Was it your local level or did this relate back to that call from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that's not clear to me because there was never an official document that came and stated that Muslims should not respond to the call-up. It was a voluntary decision by each conscript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And did not Mr. Izetbegovic state this publicly, that he would not let his son respond to the call-up, he wouldn't tell him to do so; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that. But I don't think that that was a crime. And I also recall that you said that one people would disappear from the earth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Mesanovic, if this is something that you happen to remember, Mr. Izetbegovic stated this in early 1991, and I, in late 1991, on the 14th or the 15th of October, begged not to go for independence before the transformation and that that would be a dangerous thing, first of all for the Muslims. Is that what you're talking about, my speech at the Assembly?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, political disagreement is not a crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Political disagreement should not influence the defence capacities of a country; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, if we are attacked from the outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know, Mr. Mesanovic, that Prijedor in the first two maps of Cutileiro's, in the first one it was supposed to be a canton made up of Muslim parts in the Sana river valley from Prijedor, Sanski Most, and Kljuc; and in the second map, the whole of Sanski Most and the whole of Prijedor was supposed to be part of the Muslim unit, the Muslim canton. Do you recall those maps, and do you know that I accepted those maps with the exception of some Serbian villages which would remain in the Banja Luka Krajina? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if all of that happened before the war, then I don't see any reason why we needed those maps in the first place. Why were there any preparations for such maps? We lived fantastically for 40 or 50 years. This is your ideology. Until you came with your ideology.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, are you saying that it was more important that I appeared or that the Muslim side decided to leave Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you have to keep in mind that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, let's come to issues. I'm struggling to understand the relevance of your lines of questioning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Excellency, I'm going through what the witness said at different times, and that seems important to me. And it can be seen from the question and the allegation by Mr. Mesanovic that my political emergence led to a disruption of our life together, and I'm saying that that was not so but that it was the decision on secession that led to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, we lived together well in Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: And in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Mesanovic testified about his detention and what he saw at the detention centre. Why don't you come to the issue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Excellency, there is again the question of what it is that I should omit of the things that the Prosecution placed in the amalgamated statement. If that can in any way damage my position, then I have to go through it. Otherwise why did not the Prosecution exclusively then deal with that? However, it's a fact that this witness was arrested, and we need to see which circumstances he was arrested in and why. It's not just Omarska. It's the entire situation that is part of his testimony in the amalgamated statement. But I will try to narrow this down now, in any case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You looked at the documents today and you also said, on page 7, that they were removed from the SDA, and so on. Do you remember that the Serbian municipality of Prijedor was proclaimed and that Cehajic began to form the Muslim municipality of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I know about the proclamation of the Serbian municipality. As for this other thing, I don't know about that. And I think that even if he had wanted to do it, it was already too late, because you had done that already very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So if there are two municipalities, Mr. Mesanovic, is it natural that Serbian jobs in the Serbian municipality would be performed by Serbian officials and not officials of the SDA who have completely opposite interests?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, provided there were two municipalities. In my view, there were not two municipalities. There was one which was legitimate and the other one which was illegitimate, that -- the Serbian municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But do you know that Mr. Cehajic agreed to cross over to the other bank of the Sana and to establish the municipality and the police force?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Mesanovic, that even with such division of the municipalities it was possible for both Muslims and Croats to work at the Serbian municipality with a proviso that they take an oath and sign the declaration that they would abide by the laws and the constitution?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Whose laws and whose constitution? To whom should they have signed this oath?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you know there that the constitution of Republika Srpska came into force on the 27th of March?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: And that means that we should have been loyal to the Serbs; is that what you're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Mesanovic, if you agreed to live in Republika Srpska and to work in its state organs, it is only natural that under new circumstances and under a new political system you would declare that you accept this new republic, its laws, and its constitution.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, that was an illegal republic in 1992. So why should I become a people out of the law, a terrorist, instead of being a normal person?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, do you know that we were given a right to constitute a republic on the 18th of March, 1992?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And that included our right to have the police and possibly the national guard, but we were entitled to have all our executive legislative branch organs, such as education, schooling, et cetera. Do you know what was envisaged by this agreement?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is all argumentative. Let's proceed to your next topic. Mr. Mesanovic already said he doesn't -- he didn't know, then there's no point of continuing that line of question. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. But then his general answers should be viewed in a different light. His saying that the Republika Srpska was an illegal entity acquires a new meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You knew that before power was taken over on the 30th of April, happened after telegram arrived from Alija Delimustafic, which requested military action to be taken against the barracks, the army depots, the JNA, and the Serbs of Prijedor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise, but, without saying yes or no, all I can say is that I know nothing about this telegram. This telegram has been mentioned in all the trials that I have been involved in so far, but I am really keen to finally see this telegram. I think this is just a fabrication, that it is product of somebody's imagination that this telegram arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 31124 of your testimony --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 1D04422, if we can call up this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- you confirmed there that you knew that power was taken over after the arrival of this telegram.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No. There may have been some mention of the telegram arriving on the 29th or 30th, but I don't say that it's being -- continuously being mentioned and putting to me in a fictitious way, but the fact is that you took over power on the 30th of April. I have never seen this telegram, and I don't think the Court has seen it either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since you were working for the SUP, you didn't receive these kind of telegrams, but did you receive this telegram or telegrams of that nature through defence lines?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us look at it, and I'm going to read in English: [In English] [As read] "All right. Now, was the immediate cause for the take-over a telegram which the head of the public security station whose name was, I think, Hasan Talundzic? "A. Talundzic, yes. "Q. He was the chief of the police in Prijedor, and this telegram was sent by Alija Delimustafic, the minister, asking for action to be taken to block the barracks, seize the weapons from the JNA, and similar acts, and that by mistake it came into the hands of the Serbs in Prijedor too. Do you know all about that? "A. No. I worked in the Secretariat for National Defence and not in the SUP. "Q. Well, that dispatch was sent on the 30th -- or, rather, 28th [sic] of April, and on 30th they took over the main institutions. Do you know about that? "A. Yes, the Serbs took control on the 30th in the morning at around 5.00." [Interpretation] Are you saying that the Chamber hasn't seen this either?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at D400, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You see the problem of complex questions here again. To which was the answer "yes" answer to. Let us proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have D400.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see to whom this is being sent? And it says here that this is the implementation of the decision of the commander of the Territorial Defence and the president of the republic's decision and it's being put into practice, and total blockage is being ordered here. You didn't know about this?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I categorically say that I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since it was dispatched through MUP lines?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I told you what I was doing before the war. I was never within those top circles, either in executive branch or in political circles.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 09042. 09042.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the Territorial Defence staff of RBH?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And we see that it is being sent to all defence and Territorial Defence organs. It says directive for defending sovereignty and independence of the republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Are you aware that Hasan Efendic issued this immediately upon his appointment?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: This is a staff of Territorial Defence of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, whereas I was under the jurisdiction of the Republican Secretariat for National Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the next page to see who the recipients are and who signed this document. We need the last page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You see where it says, under item 4 which says "I have decided," and here we see who the recipients are; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. TO, TO, TO, TO, TO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you're trying to say that the TO had never received this telegram?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No, they hadn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then we are going to tender this through another witness. Do you know that the Muslims themselves sent this to me the very following day because they were concerned about this, they admitted that this had come from them, and they were surprised that it arrived on my desk so soon?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. You said that you did receive it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember me publicising this?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you say, on the 30th, a propaganda campaign was launched. Do you agree, Mr. Mesanovic, that the Muslim position vis-à-vis the conference and the defence of the country and the unity of the country was diametrically opposed to that of the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know in which respect particularly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the Muslim side bent on leaving Yugoslavia at any cost? Did they first accept the Lisbon Agreement and after that rejected it in the hope of seeing the Serbs giving up on their ideas and that they would have a unified Bosnia under their full control? Were those the difference between Muslims and Serbs?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I never attended any talks between you or Izetbegovic or any other people involved in those games.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said today that you had been sent to be on standby until further notice. You often confuse that with dismissal. Is it true that you were sent home to be on standby and that they were -- that you were recalled to come back to work at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I was sent home to be on standby on the 22nd, just like the other seven people. I was called back because they couldn't find an adequate replacement for me. When I finished my job, I was arrested. So officially my employment was not terminated on the 22nd because I didn't receive any written decision. There was just this gap. I needed a couple of days more because I was on the list for arrest on the 14th of June, but they gave me this grace period of ten more days in order for me to be able to complete my job. All these decisions that they issued are worthless. What about those people who were killed and people who never received any decisions?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's stick to your experience. Can you tell me, please, how far is Banja Luka from Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: 54 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And was the system of communication, telephone communications, and transportational links more or less operational?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: In what period?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From April until May.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please pause between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's impossible for the interpreters if you overlap to such a degree. Let's start again. From April until May; that was the question. And, Mr. Mesanovic, could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From the outbreak of conflict in Sarajevo in April until the date of your arrest, did you have telephone lines with Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the answer because it was overlapping.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, your answer was what? Could you repeat the answer. They didn't hear your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not on a daily basis, as far as telephone connections are concerned. But as for transportation links, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that there was a Rudi Cajavec factory in Banja Luka, that there were many people who were expert in IT, and that you were their only recourse?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before your arrest. You said that -- Your answer was "yes" but it was not recorded. The question was: Were you offered, although you were never forced, to sign a solemn declaration or a pledge, call it what you will, to the Serbian municipality and to remain in work?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And then you said that already on the 3rd of May a check-point was set up by the patriotic league and the defence of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's contained in your evidence given in the President Milosevic trial on the 20th of January, 2004, page 31147.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D4422.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said that Omarska and a number of Serbian villages came under blockade.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, who said that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are we going to see the Milosevic transcript? Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Lines 10 to 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at your answer: [In English] "I don't know where else it could have been. After Kozarac, you have Serb villages, Lamovita, Omarska, and so on." Then there was a question: "Q. ... blocked; is that right? "A. Yes, that's right ... but ... that's what the Serb authorities said. "Q. And you don't know about it [sic]? "A. Well, I wasn't there." [Interpretation] And so on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued] ... here again, Mr. Karadzic, I don't think witness can confirm the fact that it was set up by a patriotic league.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're going to find it. Who else could have set it up other than the patriotic league and the Defence of Kozarac? And the end he said "I heard about --"

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If it is convenient, we can take a break now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: For half an hour. And resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, let's try and recapitulate. Will you agree that regardless of the events in Bosanski Brod of the 26th of March, in Bijeljina of the 31st of March, in Kupres, et cetera, that the war broke out in Sarajevo on the 6th of April?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I believe that that is true. That's when the incident happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So regardless of the telegram of the 12th of April, which you didn't see, all the way through to the 30th of April, more or less, there were no significant events occurring in your area; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then on the 30th of April the Serbs took over power, you were not aware of the fact that Cehajic wanted to set up a municipality; you weren't aware of these issues?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then all the way through to the 22nd of May until the ambush at the Hambarine check-point, and the incident where two Serb reservists were killed, two seriously wounded, two lightly wounded, in that period there weren't significant events happening; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then there came about the call to surrender weapons and the crisis surrounding Kozarac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 22nd of May, you are sent home, where your status of employment is frozen; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then we have the 30th of April. Is it true that on the 30th of April the Green Berets, the Patriotic League, the various units of Territorial Defence of various localities more or less under the command of Ecimovic mount an attack on Prijedor from various directions?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Not on the 30th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 30th of May?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was there and I felt it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree that throughout that day, and possibly even on the next, there were skirmishes, there was fighting going on in the town and possibly around it as well?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what was going on in the town. I heard shooting, I heard explosions, and I saw smoke. What was actually going on, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you recall that Radio Prijedor broadcast a message to the effect that those who were not involved in fighting should stay in their homes and that these homes where nobody would be involved in any fire should hang up white sheets?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Radio Prijedor did make an announcement for all the family homes, including flats, that they should place some sort of white cloth or sheet. They should hang them outside their windows, and that this would be a sure sign of where no fight would be forthcoming.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And were Serb soldiers marked with white ribbons?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And did the Serbs fire at those who had ribbons by way of a marking?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is where the problem arises, Witness, when you start thinking about it. Is it not true that they made an announcement that those who do not intend to take part in the fighting or shooting should hang out a white symbol of sorts?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, but how come it was only us who had to set ourselves apart by certain markings and not the Serbs as well? Why was it just the Muslims? Why weren't the Serbs called upon to hang out white sheets?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who specified that it was just to be the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: It was the radio broadcast that mentioned only the Muslims. I cannot quote what Radio Prijedor broadcast word for word, but I know for that fact there was no mention for the need for the Serbs to hang out white sheets from their windows.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And, Mr. Mesanovic, what was the reason stated behind this request?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I really can't be called upon to quote the exact words of what happened in -- on the 30th of May, 1992. I only know that we were supposed to mark off specifically homes, gates, front doors. What I'm not clear on is why only we were called upon to do that and not you as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll deal with it later. Was it not also requested of the population that they should stay in their homes, not get involved in fighting? Was that not the case?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, yes, when the fighting subsided, all these civilians were rounded up in their individual homes, put on buses, and taken to --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the name. Can the witness repeat the last part of his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You know what happens when -- when you have a situation of chaos where you can't stop to think, you merely round up everyone, and then you conduct triage; is that how it was done?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Everybody was rounded up and taken to Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were looking at this document today which was adopted. Give me a moment. It's part of your amalgamated statement at page 54475. Where it is stated that all the Serbs who were -- is it 38? Yes, 38 amalgamated statement. So you do recall that you said that there was this decision dated the 2nd of June, a day after the fighting ended, the decision was issued which said, "all Serbs who have been in prison by mistake are hereby released from further imprisonment." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Can I have a look at that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Page 38, and these are minutes of the meeting held on the 2nd of June, 1992. It was a meeting of the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Prijedor, which adopted a series of decisions on the release of detainees. Do you recall that there were Serbs among them who had not been apprehended by mistake and who stayed in detention?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Item 2 states: "All military personnel -- all soldiers and military personnel who have been detained by mistake while actually on leave with the authorization of appropriate military authorities are hereby released from further imprisonment." So you were aware of this?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So first they round them up on and then on the following day they proceeded to do the triage; right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Because it so happened that a number of Serbs were among those rounded up, one, two, or three of them. But most of the population in that part of town were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The question as I put it was not recorded properly, so they -- as they were rounding them up from their homes, they were not conducting triage. It was on the following day that they proceeded to do so; right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Probably so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It then goes on to say that those aged 60 and over who are shown not to have committed any infraction are to be released forthwith; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if that's what you are reading, I suppose that's what it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Item 5 goes on to say -- Article 5 goes on to say that all those prisoners who, in a legal procedure carried out by competent organs, are found not to be guilty are to be released forthwith; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: That's not something that I saw happen in reality, either the competence or the release from Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we will sort it out quite nicely now, Mr. Mesanovic. Were you examined by inspectors once and twice, once in the presence of an experienced inspector and the second time it was a not-so-competent inspector?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you were questioned about information that they had come by in some other examinations?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, no. Both these inspectors, professional policemen who were examining me, were incompetent, and they were asking me about nonsense.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll see about that. You were in the MUP building, were you not?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please make a pause.

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was the size of the detention unit in that building? How many people could be detained there?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't know what the standards were. The room was 5 by 6, perhaps, with a protrusion in one of the walls, without toilet facilities. There was a bed frame, a couple of blankets, and there were eight of us there when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This was the detention unit in the public security station and it could not accommodate more individuals, could it have?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure that if they had more people, they would have pushed them in. I don't think they really cared about standards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. So when they apprehended close to 3,000 individuals, could they have put them into the public security station and examined them there?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When they put them up in Keraterm and realised that the facility there were too small, did they not open up Omarska?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I couldn't specifically tell you how many individuals were held in Keraterm because I wasn't there and I don't know who had been apprehended before the 30th. I suppose it was a multitude of individuals who had to be put up somewhere safely. I think that they cared mostly about safety and security, rather than the premises they chose.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You testified about the fact that the inspectors came at 8.00 and left at 5.00; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
