utterances.text: You also testified that there were different shifts of people, some of which were quite cruel, engaging in harassment, and even murder of people; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So how did you explain what the difference was about, and I mean the difference in the various shifts of people?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's probably dependent on the people, the guards who made up a shift. All of us are different, some a bit better, some worse.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You say that among them there were drunkards, psychopaths, and that these shifts were unbearable?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I don't want to talk about psychopaths. I can't speak about that. But there were definitely drunkards. And if we're talking in terms of psychopaths, then I can tell you that all of them were psychopaths.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well, you say that they would beat people up once the inspectors had left; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KERIM MESANOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At page 38, you say -- a moment, please. Have a look at that page: [In English] "Going back to Article 1 of the decision, 'all Serbs who have been imprisoned by mistake are hereby released from further imprisonment.' Do you see any reference to Muslims or non-Serbs who have been imprisoned by mistake, whether they are hereby released from further imprisonment?"

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: being released. Only Serbs are being released from further imprisonment." [Interpretation] Do you stand by that statement today?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, do you know that out of these detention units and investigation prison in Prijedor, 59 per cent were released and 41 per cent were sent to Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Are you talking about the 6th of August and the point when Omarska was closed, or are we talking about the period while it was still in existence?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm asking about the period when it still existed. Were not people released gradually even as the investigation unfolded?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Let's make things clear. As you say, 59 per cent were released on the 6th of August to Prijedor, and then 41 were released to Manjaca, and only a hundred were -- stayed behind in order to take pictures of them in pajamas, in proper beds, and having a meal. But during the one and a half months of the existence of Omarska, the 45 days that I spent there, I know only of two individuals having left Omarska. And they were dead.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch their names.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And both of these supposedly died of natural causes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, I think that the sarcasm is not necessary. Our war was cruel enough, so that there is no need to leave out the truth. The truth is black enough as it is. If you want to be a witness, you need to show a little bit of objectivity.

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: I apologise. First of all I'm a victim, and then I'm a witness. And I'm telling you what -- and what I'm saying is the truth. The beginning of the war, May, June, July, at the beginning, in Prijedor, not a single bullet was fired, as far as I know, by those who were expelled, beaten, raped, all their property was confiscated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: One by one. How come no bullet was fired when Prijedor, on the 30th of May, was attacked from four directions?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Because I had began to work after that attack. There was a story about the infamous hand-grenade which dropped in front of the SUP, and if you know what a bomb is, then you know that a small crater has to be left behind. There was no crater. There was nothing on the wall, on the window. On the 30th, all the Muslim homes were demolished. No Serbian homes were demolished or damaged in the fighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We are going to go back to that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please look at --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And could Mr. Karadzic please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, you referred to the two individuals who left Omarska and died. The interpreters couldn't catch the names. Could you repeat the names, kindly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] One of them was Safet Ramadanovic. He was a private businessman from Prijedor, an elderly man. He was older than 60. The second one was Ganic. He also was older than 60. They were carried out in coffins. They died of natural causes after a beating. And the TV said that it was due to natural causes, but I actually saw them being beaten, or after they were beaten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic, could you repeat the number of the document you want to show us.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D04428.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Dr. Ibrahim Beglerbegovic is?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes, I do. He was released from Omarska. He was in Omarska for a day or two, I can't remember exactly, but he was released from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Alive?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes, alive. I skipped over one individual in a cycle of 5- to 6,000 people. And if that is a good deed, then I apologise for all that I have said. To release one person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, it's not about good deeds. It's about the fact that he was arrested by mistake. This is a confirmation from the MUP and from the Ministry of Defence that this is to certify that Mr. Beglerbegovic was erroneously detained and that he was being sent to work duty and there are instructions that he should not be touched by anyone?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. But the date is 1995. We're talking about 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about the top confirmation or certificate?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Oh, the one at the top. I'm sorry, I didn't see that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's from the 24th of July.

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the 24th of July, it says captured or detained by mistake?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes, that is right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we tender this document, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it says that it was a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1745, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You have just now mentioned the question of property, so I have to deviate from my line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 03584. This is 1D.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Mesanovic, do you see that on that same, the 2nd of June, 1992, the Crisis Staff issued an order to prevent looting and robbing and to protect private and socially owned property?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we tender this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Is Mr. Karadzic going to put a question to the witness about the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What was your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question was, does he see that on the same day, the 2nd of June, in terms of what the witness said about the confiscation of property, the Crisis Staff issued an order that improperly taken property should be returned and that private and socially owned property should be protected from robbery and looting, and he confirmed that that is what the document states, which was issued at that time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So according to this document, I can reclaim and have all of my property returned to me, and all the others too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who took your property from you, Mr. Mesanovic?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Well, I don't know their first and last name. It was the SDS Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was your property confiscated or looted?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Well, I was driven out and everything stayed in their hands, as they called it. I voluntarily signed that I was voluntarily leaving, but actually I escaped and my wife signed that form.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we will come to that. But as for your property, was it taken away by some kind of legal document or did it stay behind and was it robbed?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: According to this, it states that the police should have protected me. I was not protected. I was left without all the things that I had after 33 years of my life and after 13 years of work. I don't know what you call that. If I was not protected and if it wasn't robbed, then it was the legal authorities who took my property.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at paragraph 1, that the authorities are aware that these are robberies or looting and they are preventing the confiscation of property?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, could you repeat your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2007, I went to court in Sarajevo, and they showed me a photograph of my car. When I, at least, asked for the photograph of my car, I wasn't allowed to have it. They said that it was a court document. Mr. Karadzic, the legal authorities did not provide any kind of paper for the things that they took from me and others. And you know very well that all the savings, all the money in the bank accounts, was -- were robbed. Why would somebody leave something behind voluntarily? Why would they be crazy to leave with only a plastic bag with a few items in their hands?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm coming back to this because you said on page 47 that the property was confiscated. Confiscation is a legally regulated way of taking away property. I'm not disputing the fact that you were robbed, but this document indicates that the authorities were aware that this was happening and this is an attempt at prevention.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we tender this.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On my part?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, no, I wouldn't have shown to you this document had you not said that this was robbery or confiscation, and I --

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: I think that it's a play on words whether it's confiscation or robbery. Me and thousands of other people were left without their property, and you can call that whatever you want.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, me too, Witness. I had a five room apartment full of all sorts of things that I no longer have. It was left behind. And we can go back and forth about the way to formulate this and play with legal terms.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we tender this.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, again it's comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unacceptable, Mr. Karadzic. We do not -- we will not admit this through this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But the witness confirmed that the -- it was not confiscation but that it was looting or robbery.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Better said that it was left behind and it was never restored to me again. I don't know how you would classify that. I have still not been able to have my property restored to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, is it true that you were told that you were prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And is it correct that Zeljko Mejakic told you that your statement is no good and that you need to change it in order -- if you wished to be released?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: I don't think that there was any question of release, but he just said that my statement was no good. It was taken by Ratko Milosavljevic, and I don't know whether that's the story that we talked about. I mean, this was a story about nice weather, conditionally speaking, and then he came to tell me that the statement was no good, that the statement would be taken again by his uncle, so I never repeated it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And is it correct that this Maric was charged - besides these 100.000 for telling secrets to Croatia, betraying secrets - for issuing military certificates relieving conscripts of the duty to serve?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Well, I don't know that was wrongly attributed to him or it's a wrong interpretation. He didn't work in the secretariat, had nothing to do with these certificates. Maric began to work -- he ended his work in 1991 when he went to Manjaca. He never worked again.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please repeat what they're saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, do you see the transcript?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So when the transcript stops moving, that's the time when you are suggested starting your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where should we start again?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thus, is it correct that you were told that Maric admitted and named you as his accomplice in these acts in relation to Croatia?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you were also charged with issuing permits which were used by military conscripts to get off serving their military term of duty?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Not from serving. There was some kind of charge regarding the failure to go to the front. I don't have the indictment. I mean, it was really whatever just they thought of to put in there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And is it correct, do you remember that the Muslim/Croat part of the Presidency declared war on the 20th of June to us and to the JNA, or, rather, to Serbia and Montenegro and the Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: I don't know about that. The restrictions were already in force. And at that time all we had was TV Banja Luka, which was under the control of the SDS. So everything that was broadcast on that a TV station, I knew. Everything else, I don't know. I still don't know to this very day, from 1992 onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But this was published before you were arrested, that war was declared against us. And you were arrested when?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: On the 24th.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The 24th. And these were the grounds for your arrest, that Stjepan Maric named you as being an accomplice of his and that were publishing or issuing. Was there anything else that you were charged with?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: I was not arrested after Maric. I was arrested before Maric was. Maric was still at liberty after I was arrested, so there is no connection between myself and between him. There are no actions, no dirty deeds. That is one thing that is certain. Had I taken information to Zagreb and put 100.000 in my pocket, I would have been an idiot to come back with that amount of money. Only an idiot would have done that. I asked at the time, I said that it was very easy to check when the hard drive disk was taken from the machine and how long it was gone. I mean, machinery is precise. But nobody paid any attention to that and they were asking for 100.000 German marks. Kozarski Vjesnik newspaper published this stupidity. Simply they needed games and preparation for what would follow later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not accusing you of having actually done that. All I'm interested in are grounds for your arrest. You said that in 1991 Maric went to Manjaca; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So he was arrested before you were; is that right?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Arrested at Manjaca and then returned home. And he was in Prijedor the whole time unemployed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But questioned?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Questioned in Omarska before. -- one day before I was, and that was when he was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Before you were arrested, one day before you were arrested, this was, and then you were arrested, and then you were told that he mentioned you in connection with him?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: I said that Maric was arrested after me and that he was interrogated the day before I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And so they did not put the third thing to you? Did they put anything else to you?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Well, yes, they talked about drugs from Germany and so on. They said I was selling it in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And did this prove to be true or did they abandon the charges?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: I have no idea what kind of criminal investigation. There was no official indictment. Zoric knew me very well. He knew my past, he knew my family. These were just stories. We were acquaintances. We were not people who don't know anything about each other. He knew everything about me, he knew where my brother was, how long, when he was coming, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, let's take it easy. It's another thing that he knew you privately. You were officially detained on suspicion of such and such a thing one day after being mentioned by Stjepan Maric. They held you and interrogated you and ultimately decided not to issue an indictment and they took you back.

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Well, I apologise. On the 24th of June, I was arrested. I don't know when Maric was arrested. Maric was interrogated on the 1st of July, I was interrogated on the 2nd of July. We were both in Omarska. There was only ten hours between the interrogation of Maric and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Without going into what Maric or anybody else did, the fact is that you were charged with a number of things but eventually they did not press any charges against you and you were set free.

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: I was set free at the same time as the others were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Had something of this turned out to be true, would you have been released?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: It is true that I was on the list for execution. That's correct. I was removed for the -- from the cooling list on the 2nd of July. That was told to me by a driver of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't get the name of the person.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, this was not based on any facts. There was just a list of people who were to be executed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The interpreters couldn't hear the names you referred to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a nickname. Brk. I don't know his name. I cannot remember it at the moment. He was the driver of Zeljko Mejakic, the camp commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you have no other proof that lists for execution existed except what you were told by Brk?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: I think I have seen a document here with a list of people who were executed. And then in September decisions were issued to the effect of conducting investigations against them. This document was shown to me either in the Brdjanin or the Milosevic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 40 of your amalgamated statement, you were asked about three different categories of detainees; right?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Those were marked as categories 1, 2, and 3. Let me ask you this: Was -- do you have the same proverb, you as Muslims, that we as Serbs have, which says that a farmer will give a son to the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please repeat the proverb.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The proverb that exists in our people says that a poorer farmer gives his son for war and a rich man gives an ox in order to get himself out of it. This has something to do with this categorisation. Do you agree that category 1 involved those who were actively involved in this combat of the 30th of May?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: No. And I confirm that because I myself never took part in this fighting. I never thought about going into fighting, and I never will. Judge Mehmedagic was accused of being a sniper, a man who was blind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the document that you discussed, you said that category 1 involved active combatants?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: And I think that I added to that people from Prijedor with higher a degree of education.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That is right sir. That's what you added. And you also mentioned some category for cooling. All these words, the cooling, the execution, and the other things that you mentioned, are they contained in that document or not?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: When did I add this, in my statement or in testimonies?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In testimonies.

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Some people were accused of being involved and taking part in the fighting. I'm not going to talk about this. However, all the people that I mentioned in category 1 included doctors, lawyers, teachers, engineers, and all of them perished. Only one doctor survived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that, sir. You know nothing about this. You have never seen anything with your own eyes. You saw the killing of Cermanic [phoen] who was a sick man, but they didn't know this. As for the rest of it, you never saw anything. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes. But Esad Mehmedagic -- Esad Sadikovic, in fact, was exhumed and he had a bullet in the back of his head. I didn't see when many of my friends were killed, but many of my friends were found in mass graves, which leads me to believe that they were executed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Here you ask a compound question again. The witness said yes, but we do not know which it was the answer to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It refers to the fact that this witness has only indirect knowledge of only one person being killed and his name --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't catch the name.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Question: Crnalic? And the witness replied: Yes. I am helping the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that right, you said yes?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As for the others, you only concluded that based on some other elements?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since we heard testimony here relating to Crnalic's murder, can you tell us what was it exactly that you saw?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: I was in the green house and I just heard gun-fire. He said that he was hot. He was sitting on a bench, he jumped out, and eventually he was shot at. That's what I saw. Only later somebody told me that that man was Crnalic, because at that time I didn't know who he was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You said he jumped through the window?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes, through the window of the "White House." And he came to the front of the "White House," sat on a bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's go back to this categorisation. In this document that speaks about three categories of detainees, is there any mention of executions or cooling lists or does it say quite clearly that category 1 involved combatants, the second those who were aiding and abetting, and the third category involves the financiers?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is document P2640. P2640. Can we briefly look at the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Temporary collection point of persons captured in combat, and so on and so forth. I'm sorry, this doesn't seem to be the document about the categories, but never mind. Then on page 41 you said that there were no killings that were committed overtly and that's the reason why you didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes, there were several of them. I think that Rizo Hadzalic was killed on the -- on the runway, on the "pista." And they all saw Rizo Hadzalic being killed. At the moment, I cannot recall how many people I saw, but I know for sure that these people never showed up again and it was never heard from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, if somebody is taken away, is it possible that this person might have been released? Or do you think that invariably this person was killed?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Particularly if a guard comes back with some of his clothes and trainers, he must have been released. This is my sarcastic remark. They were taken to the mine pit. They were never taken either to a road or to a station, and no vehicles entered the compound.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But these are all just your conclusions?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: No, I needn't need more than that. Ten people that disappeared is quite enough. And eventually they were discovered in mass graves. Therefore, those people were killed. They were not taken anywhere else, to the airport or some other place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, I'm asking you again: Was that your conclusion or did you see it yourself?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you have ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You have confirmed that only on two occasions you were maltreated and beaten; once you were beaten with a hard implement and the second time you were slapped on the face.

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes, it's good that it was only twice. I should have been beaten more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please do not blame me for that. I just wanted to make sure that if I -- that I read it correctly that this happened on two occasions only.

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On page 21 of your statement, you said that already in May 5th, 6th, or 10th May one could feel that authorities of the autonomous region of Krajina were in operation.

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Is that what I said, or did you read it from the transcript?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here in paragraph 16, page 21, Ms. Sutherland asked you this: [In English] "Does it say there that instructions and decisions are being forwarded from the top, and the functions of the government at the level of Krajina can now be felt?" [Interpretation] And you said yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: I think that she asked me about the documents. These are not my words. If we can locate this document, that's what I read from the document. That's not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you identified the document that contains this statement.

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: I read the document that reads this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's evident from the reading of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So you were issued a pass. And whenever it was necessary, you were given an escort as well. On page 22, you speak about the need for that, for you to have free movement, and sometimes they will send a car for you because there were drunken people around who could jeopardise your security and safety; right?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: I received the pass because I demonstrated certain level of fear at the secretariat, because I told them that I was well known in the town and that I can't go around without being noticed. And secondly, I asked for a driver to be given to me because even with a pass people knew who I was. I think that this pass actually was rather worthless. And it is true, I was given an escort.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you did get the escort?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Up until the time when Mr. Maric was interrogated, it seems that you were held in high regard by the Serbs. You got a pass, you got an escort, you were invited to come back to work; is that right?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes. But I don't think that they held me in so much higher regard. I was just a good worker. You can see how highly they regarded me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You also said that you never saw dead bodies and that all the three commanders were dismissed at various times. Just a moment. On page 36 of your amalgamated statement where you describe the beatings, you said that you never saw any shift commander being present when this was happening; is that right?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you trying to say that those who committed this were hiding this?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: No, because they had documents. They would come into rooms with those papers in their hands. They would call out people's names and take them out. They never came and took anyone randomly out. They would come with a proper piece of paper. They would read out their name. So you would get up and go out, maybe for the last time. Maybe you would survive for a few times more. So they didn't do it on a whim. They definitely did it on somebody's order, because full names were written on those pieces of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know who ordered this?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: I said somebody's order. Probably after the investigators left, apparently only Ranko Mijic, the chief of the criminal investigation department, could have left this list with someone to execute it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you are just guessing, Witness?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: No, I'm not guessing. Somebody must have ordered a piece of paper to be issued with a specific name on it. So they were very particular about it. It was not random.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were you beaten in the same way or were you beaten randomly?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: I was beaten during interrogation. I was beaten on SUP premises. So it just didn't happen like that. Somebody ordered me to be beaten. I was 37 years of age when I lost my teeth, Mr. Karadzic, and that is disability.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, I'm asking you: Did anyone came with your name, did they call you -- out your name, or did it happen just like that?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: No, not my name. But in 90 per cent of the cases, they had specific names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who did these guards report directly to?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: I think that there was the usual hierarchy, which means that they reported to the shift commander, the shift commander to the camp commander, and the camp commander to the chief of SJB, Zeljko Drljaca, Simo Mejakic [as interpreted], and the guards, and we were the end users.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You seem to make a distinction between the various shifts. Would this distinction be based on the shift leader or guards commander?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't be able to tell who made the choice of the various shifts. Was it the commanders who were assigned these men? Possibly. The commanders somehow did make an influence on the way their subordinates would behave.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you do say that there was no beating as far as the commanders were concerned.

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: No. At least not that I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's your last question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You spent a short period of time in Trnopolje and went home from there. Was it difficult to get your name on the lists of those intended to leave Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Well, yes. But let me tell you that I left Trnopolje simply because Zeljko Mejakic had me released. He took me home and I spent the night at home and then he took me back to his village, where I spent the period through to the second half of September. And I don't want to go into my relationship with Zeljko Mejakic, I discussed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then you took a number of steps to leave Prijedor; can you tell us what it was?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Well, I had a fake ID made for me, I sat on a bus with the Serbs from Omarska, and I went to Backa Palanka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if this was my last question, then that's what it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Just very briefly, Your Honour. Two questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Mr. Mesanovic, earlier today, at page 39, Mr. Karadzic asked you, put this to you: "And then all the way through to the 22nd of May until the ambush at the Hambarine check-point, and the incident where two Serb reservists were killed, two seriously wounded, two lightly wounded, in that period there weren't significant events happening; is that right?" And you said: "Yes." Were you agreeing with his assertion that there was an ambush at the Hambarine check-point?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: What I know is what I told you, because it happened. But this was a story that I heard over the radio, Radio Prijedor, and what I heard at the Secretariat for National Defence, that this was provoked by the reservists who were intoxicated and were on a rampage, in fact. And they opened fire at the check-point. Apparently guards were installed in all the various villages, including this one, and that's how the shooting came about. But I think it was staged. There were Croats there. There were Serbs. But, of course, since it was they who produced the report ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: And secondly, a couple of questions later, Mr. Karadzic said: "Then we have the 30th of April. Is it true that on the 30th of April the Green Berets, the Patriotic League, the various units of Territorial Defence of various localities more or less under the command of Ecimovic mount an attack on Prijedor from various directions?" And then --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 30th of May. It's a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: If I can finish.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Then you said: "Not on the 30th of April." Mr. Karadzic then said: "On the 30th of May?" And you said: "Yes. I was there and I felt it." Were you agreeing that on the 30th of May it was an attack by the Green Berets and the Patriotic League and various units of the TO, all those three groups?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: The question was a compound one, so I answer the first part of it. The shooting took place on the 30th of May. I said that I didn't know who the parties involved were. This was the only incident, if it occurred at all. There was nothing that followed. But because the question was compound, I suppose I answered the first part of the question, that it did indeed happen on the 30th of May. I said that all the Muslim houses were destroyed, whereas not a single Serb house was grazed by a bullet. It was only Muslim houses that were burned to the ground. My uncle's house, which stood across from Radio Prijedor, had been razed to the ground. The answer to the questions raised what was that Radio Prijedor had come under attack from house. And I did go later to check the condition of the Radio Prijedor building, while it was intact. What I said in that context was that everything was stage managed, because all those who got killed in the attack on Prijedor were policemen from Bosanski Novi and not from Prijedor. What I heard from the Serbs were that these were, in fact, individuals who had been killed in the front line and from the Banja Luka refrigerator unit were transported to Prijedor, but this is a rather more complex story, as is everything that has to do with the events in Prijedor in 1992, because, as I said, not a single bullet was fired. And if there was an attack mounted, then they would be the ones to know about it, since it was all the Muslim houses that perished in that attack. All the mosques, all the Catholic churches.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you, Mr. Mesanovic. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I have one question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In relation to what, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Witness said that radio Prijedor broadcast that they were intoxicated. And this was a fact established, that there were two Croats and four Serbs in the car and that fire was opened on them. Now, the second question is -- was, did the Serbian army come under fire from homes? It is not true that Radio Prijedor broadcast that they were intoxicated. In fact, that was supposed to be my question. Further Cross-examination by Mr. Karadzic:

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did Radio Prijedor make broadcast to the effect that they were intoxicated, that they were drunk?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Yes. And, in fact, this was a broadcast that was not aired again. And it was a story that came from one of the wounded who was in the Prijedor hospital. And the whole thing came about quite accidently.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Did -- was fire opened on the Serbian army from Serbian homes?

utterances.speaker: "No, I don't see anywhere that non-Serbs or Muslims are
utterances.text: Well, I tell you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's it. Ms. Sutherland, nothing else?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Mesanovic, that concludes your evidence. Unless my colleagues have a question for you, that concludes your evidence. And on behalf of this Chamber and the Tribunal, I would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague again to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given the time, we'll take a break for an hour now and resume at ten past 1.00 and begin with the next witness. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.10 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If the witness could take the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please take a seat and make yourself comfortable. Yes, Ms. Hildegard -- I'm sorry. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. I know that my name is not so easy.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir, can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sir, during your testimony here you will be referred to with the pseudonym KDZ017.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Can we please have Exhibit 19848 displayed on the screen, but not broadcast, please. And as it is coming up, it is the pseudonym sheet used in th Krnojelac case for this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sir, the name listed as the first and the date next to it, is that your name and date of birth?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I request the admittance of this exhibit. It needs to be under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, it will be done.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, we do not only need it for the witness name but also as a reference document, because in the Krnojelac testimony the witness makes reference to the numbers on this sheet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Sorry. That will be Exhibit P3566 under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you testified before this Tribunal in the case against Milorad Krnojelac on the 12th and 13th of February, 2001; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Have you had an opportunity to review this testimony when you prepared for your testimony in this case here?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes, I have had that opportunity. I've reviewed it all, and it's all clear.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And can you affirm that the testimony correctly reflects the evidence you provided in the -- to the Tribunal in the Krnojelac case?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: And, Mr. Witness, would you provide that same evidence to the Court if questioned on the same matters here today?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes. Quite certainly I would be able to say what I stated the first time around.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to tender this testimony as 65 ter 22062A for admittance under Rule 92 ter, and it needs to be under seal. And a public version is uploaded as 65 ter 22062B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Both will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, the under seal version will be Exhibit P3567, and the public redacted version will be Exhibit P3568.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your permission, I would like to read now a brief summary of the witness evidence in the Krnojelac case. In April 1992, Witness KDZ017, left Foca and went with his family to Montenegro where he and many other refugees from Bosnia and Herzegovina were arrested in May 1992 and transferred back to Foca. The witness was subsequently detained in the Foca KP Dom prison where he stayed with other non-Serb detainees under living conditions characterised by hunger, coldness, unhygienic conditions, and abuse which had short and long term effects on the detainee's physical and psychological health. The detainees were civilians, including old and sick people. Due to the lack of medical care and medicine, several detainees died in the prison. During his detention, the witness observed a pattern of mistreatment. Detainees were called from their rooms, taken to the administrative building, interrogated, and beaten. On four occasions in June 1992, each time several detainees were taken from their cells and beaten in a specific room in the administration building. After the beatings, single shots were heard and the sound of a truck. The victims of these events were never seen again. The witness himself was also beaten on several occasions. The witness noticed the disappearance of detainees without any trace when taken out in so-called "exchanges." The witness and many other detainees were subjected to forced labour, including work in the Miljevina mine. In October 1994, the witness and 61 other detainees were transferred to the Kula prison and subsequently exchanged in Sarajevo. Your Honour, this concludes the summary.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, on page 2902 in your Krnojelac testimony, you mentioned that you saw the camp commander, Mr. Krnojelac, together with Velibor Ostojic and Vojo Maksimovic, in front of the Ribarski restaurant in the end of 1991, beginning 1992. At that time, was there anything particular happening in that restaurant?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: With the arrival of Velibor Ostojic and Vojislav Maksimovic -- well, let me tell you first that the SDS and its followers - I can't claim that they were all members - regularly held meetings in that restaurant, Ribarski.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you. And you also mentioned on page 2940 that you saw Vojo Maksimovic, Velibor Ostojic, and Miro Stanic, and some other persons in the vicinity of a coffee shop near your office in 1991. Do you know what they were doing in Foca at that time and why they were at this particular place?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: I think that there was an error in the statement, because it was not a coffee shop. It was a private flat. The offices were close to Miso Petkovic's flat. And Miso Petkovic, Vojislav Maksimovic, and Velibor Ostojic were good friends and had been socialising before. I think it was about 9.00, as I was about to have my breakfast, that I observed the street being cordoned off at both ends. I recall having to take a different route to go to the shop. So I saw Velibor Ostojic, Vojo Maksimovic, and Miso Petkovic together getting out of a car and entering the building where Miso Petkovic had his flat.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sir, was Velibor Ostojic in Foca during the attack in April 1992? And I think it's safer, Your Honour, to go into private session for the answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, I request the admission of the associated exhibits, with two exceptions. The exhibits are set out in the table, in the 92 ter notification, but the statement identified as number 08897 will not be tendered, and the annotated floor-plan is already an exhibit. It is P3352. And the photos listed in that table are part of the big photo documentation with which is partly admitted under P3353, but I suggest to admit those as a new set under 65 ter number 11289B because they are completely different from the one admitted with the previous witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So I checked the 11289 and found out that it's a 155-pages document, but you --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But you produced six documents -- six photos in that separate number?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And we admitted the pseudonym sheet already. And I take it there's no position from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: We don't object, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll give that six photos a -- one number. One number, which will be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3569, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And that's it?

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, your evidence in the previous trial has been admitted in its entirety in lieu of your examination-in-chief, and you will be further asked by Mr. Karadzic in his cross-examination. Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You stated that you learned all these things from Mr. Lojo. Did you personally see anything of the events that you described today or was it all described to you by Mr. Lojo?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: The meetings or, rather, the negotiations that were being held with regard to the evacuation of the civilians, the cease-fire and other things, are all the -- is all the information that I got from Mr. Lojo. But what I said a minute ago when I said I saw Velibor Ostojic, Vojislav Maksimovic at the flat of Miso Petkovic, that's something that I personally witnessed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Mr. Lojo tell you that only once, or did he recount that on several separate occasions?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Well, they held meetings every day, starting from the 8th until I was in Foca, which is the 12th of April. We were in regular contact. I believe that these negotiations were held on different dates and at different times. It didn't all happen at once.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm waiting, and could you also please wait, until the interpretation is finished, then you can start your answer and vice-versa. We both need to make pauses. Where did you used to meet Mr. Lojo?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: We used to live in the same neighbourhood, 50 metres apart.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you visit each other in your flats?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes, we met both in his flat and my flat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were the Serbs spying on you? Did they notice that you were holding meetings with him?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Not that I was able to notice. But I assume that was the case, although we had been friends for 20 years. I was definitely not under suspicion because I was not politically active, but I'm sure that they were monitoring the situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Today, on page 73 of the transcript, you said that Maksimovic, Ostojic - and who was the third man? - in whose flat they were had been friends from before; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes, it is. I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You saw them alighting from a car. Did they just come out openly, or were they hiding?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: There was no need for them to hide. This was before the war. But the euphoria of the war was already in the air, and they were often together. That moment that I described, I saw them coming out of the car, but I just couldn't understand why guards or obstacles were needed or roadblocks were needed at both ends of the street where Mr. Petkovic's apartment building was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you don't think that there was anything wrong with them meeting, being all friends, but you think and you think it's not a good thing that such a high level of security was provided?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of public offices did Mr. Maksimovic and Mr. Ostojic hold?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: I know that Mr. Ostojic was the minister of information. As for Vojislav Maksimovic, I don't know. He used to work as a teacher at the Official Gazette. That's all I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that Mr. Ostojic was beaten by the Muslims at Ilidza and he ended up in hospital and then the police ordered an escort to be provided for him, do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: I heard about this incident, but I don't think that that happened during the war. I think it happened before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. He was beaten up before the war, he was given escort before the war, and you saw him before the war, in the incident that you described?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes, that's right, before the war. As for how he was beaten up, there were various different versions of the incident. I don't think that that was provoked by an ethnic revenge or something like that. I think that there was some private and personal reasons underlying this attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, this is a cynical remark concerning this incident. What leads you to believe that? Because this happened 70 kilometres from Foca, because that's the distance between Foca and Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: 70 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Based on what do you think that something else was the reason?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Because I was following the reports in the media. There were various reports appearing there, so I was never in a position to know the true information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that Professor Vojislav Maksimovic, an academician, was at the time a deputy in the Joint Assembly and the president of the caucus of Serbian deputies, did you know any of that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: No, I didn't, although I knew Maksimovic before the war for some 20 or 25 years. However, I was simply not interested in politics. I didn't follow any meetings of either political party. And I can tell you right away that as far as that question is concerned, I can't tell you anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Nevertheless, you noticed old friends getting together, just like you got together with Lojo, only the two that you mentioned were in high government position and they had their security details with them who blocked the street. Did we clarify this matter now?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: If I tell you that Vojislav Maksimovic was an extremely good friend with my father, before the war in 1991, somewhere around new year, Vojislav Maksimovic severed all friendly relations with my father. Before that, they would speak every day on the phone. And they spent every weekend together without fail. And this is a kind of indication in my mind that they actually discarded their old friends and friendships.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Was that the only friendship that broke down in Bosnia after the cessation of Bosnia from Yugoslavia was made public, or was that a frequent occurrence?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes. But that was one of the most striking examples. I know other Serb friends who up until the very beginning of the war were at least kind and polite, would stop me on the street and chat with me. And I didn't see any major disruptions in friendships.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff asked you whether at that time they were in Foca and she ascribed certain significance to that, let us clarify this for the Chamber. Is it correct that both of them are the natives of Foca and at that time they had their families living in Foca and that they had their domicile addresses there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes, it is true that both of them are from Foca. But if you take Velibor Ostojic, whom I saw twice in a hotel during a business meeting, I could not exactly notice if he was very much fond of his native town and his family.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know what happened on the evening of the 4th of April in Sarajevo, and do you know that neither of them dared stay in the town, but had to leave and to finally arrive in their native town of Foca?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: I don't know what happened in April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will tell you what happened. The Green Berets, the gun-fire, the terror, the horrible events, all of this happened in Sarajevo on the night between the 4th and the 5th. Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this Zdravko Elez still alive?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: I suppose so. He was a young person, so I surmise that he is alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And you have no objection to our attempt to try and verify your story relating to this person?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: No, I have no objection whatsoever, provided he tells the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Today, on page 74 of the transcript, you said that the real war broke out in Foca on the 8th of April; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes, on the 8th of April. Because on the 6th of April I was forced, because I saw what was afoot, I was forced to seek shelter with my family on the nearby hill, because on the 8th of April the real war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Between whom?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Between the Serbs and the Muslims. But first of all, Foca was surrounded. There was heavy artillery. There were trenches from all sides. Only one part on the left-hand side of the Drina where there was a Muslim quarter, I believe that was the only part that was defended by the Muslims. Everything else was under the Serb control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We are going to discuss the disposition and the might of all the sides involved. But I would like to know, is it possible for a war to be waged by only one side, or does it take two to wage a war?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Of course it takes two to wage a war, but this war was caused by the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at document 1D4420.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: -- you said that Serbs had their own taverns that they frequented. Was that the same situation with the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: There was total separation before the war. Everybody had their own cafes in their respective parts of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you just said something that was completely understandable. So these two ethnic communities drifted apart and they became homogenized and there was less intermingling; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: This needs to -- I hope this is not broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I checked it, it wasn't broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Okay, good. Because the name is seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You spoke about that on page 2, but you only refer to the Serbs. Now you told us that that was the situation on both sides. Is it true that Muslims used to gather together at Zios [phoen] cafe?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Zios? No, I'm not familiar with that. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there such a cafe, Zios?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes, there was, but I very much doubt that they could get together there, because part of the bus station where this cafe was located, that was the main and the focal point for the Serbs who met there. There were two Serbian restaurants, actually, where they assembled, and I really very much doubt that anyone would have courage to meet there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where did the Muslims meet?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: In Donje Polje because that was a majority populated neighbourhood, Muslim majority populated neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And was it, earlier, just a normal thing that everybody would build apartments in their own neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: No, apartments were built throughout the whole town. It wasn't a question of whether a Serb or a Muslim lived in any particular part of town, in a street, or a building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you said that Donje Polje was Muslim majority. Is it correct that there were parts of the Foca town and the Foca municipality which were predominantly, if not purely, Serb, or predominantly or purely Muslim?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Well, it's my assumption that the Muslims withdrew to Donje Polje because that was the only way out for them towards their own people. I don't know if the lines were there or not. But anyway, it was towards the Ustikolina area. That was the only way out, for fighters and civilians to be able to withdraw to that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will come to that. Do you know that there were agreements and talks about forming two municipalities whereby the Serbs and Muslims would also have a part of the town itself as well as their villages with administrative links to their own municipality?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The place where you worked, you never heard that there were negotiations about the forming of two municipalities?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: No. No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who Alija Siljak is?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you able to tell the Trial Chamber who that is?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Alija Siljak is, well, a no-good layabout. An oaf. Maybe that's too rough. But anyway, he was prone to drinking, he was homeless. I don't know what else I could say. That's how I know him, at least.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know what he was doing and is he of interest to you from the security point of view? Do you know what he was involved with?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: All I know is that Alija Siljak was briefly employed at Focatrans. And because of his irresponsible attitude and excessive consumption of alcohol, he lost that job. As for his activities during the war, all I know is that he went to Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you know that from Croatia he handled the formation and the training of HOS and the SDA units in Foca?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: I did hear that information, but I cannot believe. I don't know that man. I don't think that he was any kind of fighter. He was a horrible man. I don't think that he had any kind of courage to do anything. I did hear about the HOS during the war while I was still in Foca. HOS is coming from Gorazde, it reached Ustikolina, and so on and so forth. However, when I left the camp, I know 100 per cent that Alija Siljak was in Croatia. He was a member of the HOS; I do know that. But he was not any kind of leader, nor did he have any sort of courage for that sort of thing. Perhaps just in words, but nothing more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. But do you agree that such brave people frequently wage war using others as proxies, and they sit in the capitals and manage it all?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. That's what the war did show.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So that we can help the Trial Chamber to understand: Do we agree that the HOS is the most extreme armed group among the Croats, the Croatian Armed Forces, they were formed by the Croatian Party of Rights, which an successor of the Ustasha movement, and that they were much more extremist than the HVO?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: I cannot confirm that because I don't know. I was not ever in danger from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know -- did you know Suad Celik?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: I didn't know Suad Celik. I didn't know him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it Sead Celik, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: No, I didn't know Sead Celik either.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know who Halid Cengic was?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Halid Cengic was working in the depot of the Zelengora company.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that his son, Hasan Cengic, was a priest and a high-level functionary of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes, I do know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And do you agree that Halid Cengic, as soon as the war broke out, became the main logistics person of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Visoko?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: I did hear that, although I'm not really going to dwell on information like that, unless I checked it. That and other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that Halid Cengic, during the socialist Yugoslavia period too, in August 1990 formed the first paramilitary formation in Bosnia in Ustikolina?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: This is the first time that I'm hearing of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember that in September 1990, before the elections, a major crisis broke out about Focatrans and that the Serbs lost their rights and work in Focatrans?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: I do know about the crisis in Focatrans. As for the Serbs losing their posts and rights, I don't know even though the Serbs caused the rebellion in that work and enterprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that -- did they cause that rebellion because they had it good or because they were bereft of rights?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Well, I don't think that the Serbs or the Muslims were particularly bereft of rights. It was the same for everything. But the initiative to form two separate enterprises was launched by the Serbian workers and, of course, later there was a broader conflicts that broke out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Trial Chamber to understand, it is correct that Focatrans was a socially owned enterprise and belonged to the workers in the self-management system?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And do you confirm or do you deny or do you not know that the Muslim side in Foca began to prepare for the war against the Serbs very early on?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: I don't think that it did.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, sir, could you repeat your answer kindly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think so, no.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D4203 now, please, in e-court. That can be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is, do we agree, on the 13th of February, 1992, from the military intelligence service, and it's sending its report and it says "establishment of the HOS training centre in the area of Foca BiH"; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. But does it not say that? Is that the document?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says, report on the establishment of HOS training centre in the area of B&H, and it was signed by Enver Pendek.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you know Enver Pendek?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please be asked to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do agree with this information. I don't confirm the contents, I'm not familiar with the document.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 3 now, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sorry, but did you say you do agree with this information or you don't agree with this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, as text, I agree with the information that is posted on the monitor. With the report.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Can we look at page 3 now, paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And can you please look at this paragraph 2, which talks about Alija Siljak and Suad or Senad Celik. Did you know Senad Celik?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: I didn't know Suad or Senad Celik. Senaid Celik is the only one that I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ah-ha. Perhaps that's the one.

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
utterances.text: No, no, not -- that one was already in Germany before the war, because that's a classmate of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you look at the second paragraph so that we can see that meeting, that he received information or a report which indicates that he has been sent to Foca, to the HOS training centre, headed by Alija Siljak. He was told to report to the cafe [indiscernible] in Foca, where he would ask for Suad or Senad Celik who would take him to the training centre some 20 kilometres from Foca in the direction of Sepan Polje, located in the deserted facilities of the forest workers." Did you know that people were being trained in a number of places in hills around Foca and that shots could be heard from there?

utterances.speaker: KDZ017
